title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the third draft of 'Analysis situs' (1986), Grothendieck axiomatizes a category-free 'domain of figures' (F, ≤, ≪). Here ≤ is inclusion of figures and ≪ is a 'refinement' relation. The intended model is closed unions of strata of a stratified space, related by subdivision or refinement. M ⊂ F is the set of 'multistrates' or elementary figures: the strictly irreducible (completely join-irreducible) elements. Each figure F has a 'déploiement' F̃ = {X∈M | X ≤ F}, its set of strata.

Page content, step by step.

(1) Order-theoretic reconstruction (end of the scholie from the previous page). Assume At1 (majorized sups exist), At2 (every figure is the sup of its strata) and At3 (below). Restrict to figures of finite type. Then (F, ≤) is equivalent to a triple (M, ≤, ≬) where:
- ≤ is an order;
- ≬ ('compatible', i.e. jointly majorized) is reflexive and symmetric;
- (a) every majorized closed (down-closed) subset of M is of finite type, i.e. a finite union of principal down-sets X̃ = M_{≤X};
- (b) ≬ is inherited downward: X ≬ Y, X' ≤ X, Y' ≤ Y ⇒ X' ≬ Y'.
Margin: F is then recovered as the set of finitely generated down-closed subsets of M whose elements are pairwise compatible.

(2) At3, the 'criterion of compatibility by strata'. If every stratum of F is compatible with every stratum of G, then F ∨ G exists. Compatibility is therefore 'coherent': pairwise consistency implies consistency.

(3) Axioms linking ≤ and ≪.
- At4: F ≪ G iff every stratum X of F satisfies X ≪ Y for some stratum Y of G. This reduces ≪ on F to ≪ on M (a lower-power-domain / Hoare-type lifting). With ≤ ⇒ ≪ on M, it gives the corollary F ≤ G ⇒ F ≪ G.
- At6, 'smallest stratum' or 'internal refinement': for X ∈ M and X ◁ F, the set F^X = {Y∈F̃ | X ≪ Y} has a least element.
- Notation: X °≪ Y ('X is an internal refinement of Y'). This means Y is the least element of Ỹ^X, i.e. X ≪ Y, and X ≪ Y' ◁ Y ⇒ Y' = Y. Equivalently X lies in the 'interior' Amb(Y)°. This is the 'carrier stratum' of a refinement, like the unique smallest cone of a coarse fan containing the relative interior of a cone of a subdivision.
- At5, 'intrinsic refinements': for compatible X, Y ∈ M, X ≪ Y ⇒ X ≤ Y. Consequently ≤ and ≪ coincide inside any F̃. Also, for compatible figures, F ≪ G ⇔ F ≤ G.
- At7: internal refinement is transitive.

(4) Translation into (M, ≤, ≪, F̃):
- At_M0: ≤ ⇒ ≪.
- At_M1: members of F̃ are down-closed.
- At_M2: F̃ is closed under down-closed subsets and contains ∅.
- At_M3: pairwise compatibility of two members implies their union is a member.

What it serves: an intrinsic, purely combinatorial 'site' of stratified figures with a refinement relation, as a foundation for a tame-topology analysis situs.
errors: Notation slip: the text says 'X est plus petit élément de Ỹ^X'. It should be 'Y is the smallest element of Ỹ^X', since X ≪ Y' ◁ Y ⇒ Y' = Y expresses minimality of Y.
At6 is written '∀X,F ∈ F'; it should read X ∈ M, F ∈ F.

In the consequence of At5, 'si F,G ∈ M et F ≬ G alors F ≪ G ⇔ F ≤ G' should have F,G ∈ F. The proof goes via At4: strata of compatible figures are compatible because they all lie under F∨G, so At5 applies stratum-wise.

The equivalence with (M, ≤, ≬) only covers figures of finite type. At1's arbitrary majorized sups then fail (infinite sups are not of finite type). Grothendieck acknowledges this on the next page: extra structure ('antifiltrations infinies') is needed for the general case.
The reconstruction also tacitly needs that elements of M are exactly the completely join-irreducible elements, and that F̃ determines F (At2). This is assumed, not stated on this page.

ideas.what: A poset of figures in which every element is the join of the completely irreducible elements below it, with coherent compatibility. It is equivalent to (M, ≤, ≬) with ≬ reflexive, symmetric and downward-inherited; figures are finite down-closed pairwise-compatible sets.
ideas.modern_name: Prime event structure with binary conflict, and its domain of (finite) configurations; prime-algebraic coherent domains (dI-domains)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel 1979/1981; Winskel 1980–82; related to Girard's coherence spaces (1986–87) and Scott information systems (1982)

ideas.what: At3: compatibility of figures is checked pairwise on strata (pairwise consistent implies a join exists).
ideas.modern_name: Coherence (pairwise-bounded sets are bounded) in domain theory; flag-complex condition for simplicial complexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Plotkin (coherent domains), Winskel; Gromov's flag condition in another setting

ideas.what: At4: the refinement relation on figures is determined stratum-wise by ∀∃ (each stratum refines some stratum).
ideas.modern_name: Hoare / lower powerdomain lifting of a preorder

ideas.what: At6 and the notion X °≪ Y: under a refinement, each fine stratum has a unique smallest coarse stratum receiving it. At7 makes this 'internal refinement' transitive; At5 says refinement between compatible strata is just inclusion.
ideas.modern_name: Carrier stratum/cell of a subdivision or refinement of stratifications (cf. fan subdivisions, simplicial subdivision carriers)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical PL topology (carrier of a subdivision); stratified spaces literature
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only sketches 'tame topology' programmatically, without this axiomatics

missed.claim: Grothendieck's finite-type 'domaine de figures' is exactly the domain of finite configurations of a prime event structure. Multistrates are events; ≤ is causality; failure of ≬ is conflict, with the inheritance axiom b). At3 is the coherence condition. He thus independently arrives at a structure central to theoretical computer science (Winskel), as a foundation for stratified tame topology. The link between combinatorial stratified-space axiomatics and event structures/coherent domains does not appear in the literature on his tame-topology program.
missed.quote: X ≬ Y, X' ≤ X, Y' ≤ Y ⇒ X' ≬ Y' ! ... F = ens des parties fermées de M, de type fini, formées d'éléments deux à deux compatibles
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The two literatures could exchange tools. Event-structure and domain-theoretic results (representation theorems, stable maps) could apply to face posets of stratified spaces and their refinements. The 'refinement' relation ≪ with carrier axioms suggests a notion of event-structure refinement akin to the action refinement studied by van Glabbeek–Goltz.

missed.claim: The axiomatization of the refinement relation ≪ via internal refinement (At4–At7) is an intrinsic, order-theoretic theory of subdivisions of stratified figures. Grothendieck leaves it unfinished; the general (non-finite-type) case requires extra 'antifiltration' data, per the next page.
missed.quote: X °≪ Y ⇔ ... X ≪ Y, et X ≪ Y' ◁ Y ⇒ Y' = Y (ou X ∈ Amb(Y)°) X raffinement interne de Y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a possible combinatorial foundation for o-minimal / tame stratification refinements and for exit-path or stratified-space combinatorics (face posets, subdivisions). No published development of these specific axioms is known.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but foundational order-theoretic axiomatics. Its main interest is that it coincides precisely with prime event structures and coherent prime-algebraic domains, apparently unnoticed, together with an original carrier-type axiomatics of refinement. Both are unpublished pieces of the tame-topology program, but not deep new theorems.
transcription_corrections: The relation symbol transcribed as '\not\asymp' is Grothendieck's compatibility symbol ≬ ('between'), as on the previous page. It means 'compatible' (sup exists), not 'not asymptotic'.
First line reads roughly 'Donc le domaine de (F, ≤) de figures de t.f. [type fini] est équivalent à : (M, ≤ (ordre), ≬ (relation réflexive symétrique))'.

Condition a) reads 'Toute partie fermée majorée de M est de type fini (i.e. réunion finie d'ensembles X̃ = M_{≤X})', with 'majorée' inserted rather than struck, consistent with the next page's 'Toute partie fermée majorée de M est de t.f.'.
The margin next to At4 reads 'Corollaire F ≤ G ⇒ F ≪ G'. The margin labels show the axiom numbers At5/At6/At7 were renumbered by overwriting.
In the definition of °≪, 'X ≪ Y' ◁ Y ⇒ Y' = Y' is the intended clause; the symbol before Y is ◁ (incidence).
